title: Cardinal Billing Account Rules Manual: Account Opening, Status and Close
content:
## Section 7. Life of a Cardinal Billing Account

7.1 **Opening.** The billing account opens with the policy on the pay plan chosen at bind, and the plan's entry gates (accepted payment methods, autopay where required, and the financial-responsibility restriction) must hold on the method on file.

7.2 **Renewals.** The account stays open through renewals of the same policy; each renewal term is billed on the plan on file.

7.3 **Close.** The account moves to closed only after the policy has ended and the final balance is settled under the refund and write-off rules; an account in collections closes when the collections balance is paid or written off.

## Account statuses and how an account moves between them

| From | To | What moves it |
|---|---|---|
| Current | Notice pending | A notice of cancellation for nonpayment is mailed and the account waits for the cure or the cancellation effective date (system) |
| Notice pending | Current | The amount required to rescind is received on or before the cancellation effective date and the notice is rescinded (system) |
| Notice pending | Cancelled for nonpayment | The cancellation effective date passes without the cure and the policy is cancelled for nonpayment (system) |
| Cancelled for nonpayment | Current | The account is reinstated after the reinstatement payment (and, where required, the signed no-loss statement) is received within the window (representative) |
| Cancelled for nonpayment | Collections | An earned-premium balance left unpaid after cancellation is referred to collections (system) |
| Cancelled for nonpayment | Closed | After the reinstatement window, the final balance is zero, refunded or written off and the account closes (system) |
| Current | Closed | The policy ended (insured cancellation, nonrenewal, expiration) and the final balance is settled (system) |
| Collections | Closed | The collections balance is paid or written off and the account closes (system) |

The account balance is the amount billed and not yet paid on the account, in US dollars; a positive balance means the customer owes, a negative balance is a credit owed to the customer.

## Entry gates, illustrated (hypothetical)

A policy bound on the Cardinal Card Autopay Monthly Plan with a bank account as the method on file does not meet that plan's accepted payment methods; with a credit card on file and autopay on, it does.
